newsitem.title: LIBERIA: African force warns ships to keep off Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: African force warns ships to keep off Sierra Leone.

text.p: A Nigerian-led military coalition said it would start enforcing a blockade of Sierra Leone on Wednesday to force coup leaders there to relinquish power.
The ECOMOG peacekeeping force, whose main base is in neighbouring Liberia, warned ships and aircraft to keep clear of Sierra Leone's territorial waters immediately.
"Any action in contravention of this warning is at the peril of the ship or aircraft," said an ECOMOG statement issued in the Liberian capital Monrovia.
The military coup in Sierra Leone which toppled elected president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah has been denounced by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
Sierra Leone's neighbours, led by regional superpower Nigeria, blockaded the country to force coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koroma and his junta colleagues to step down.
Talks between junta envoys and a West African ministerial committee to resolve the crisis broke down last weekend when Koroma defiantly announced he would stay in power until 2001.
Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha, the head of the 16-nation Economic Community of West African States, on Saturday signalled tougher action on Sierra Leone.
At the inauguration of a new president in Liberia marking the end of a seven-year civil war there, Abacha said there could be no lasting peace in Liberia without security in Sierra Leone.
He called for international coopeartion in enforcing sanctions against the Freetown junta.
ECOMOG's statement followed the weekend docking in Freetown of a Russian-flag ship with rice and a Panamanian-registered vessel with fuel oil in violation of the embargo.
The embargo has already caused severe shortages in Freetown, where most shops, banks and commercial houses remain closed since the coup which was followed by massive looting.
There are few taxis on the road and most people are having to walk everywhere. Petrol on the black market is said to be three times the pre-coup cost.
Power cuts have become the norm, but oil industry source said the weekend shipment of fuel oil would not do much to improve that situation.
